title: Felicity
type: Player character · battle maid and practical caregiver
dek: Quick to face physical danger, slower to claim the right to decide, and increasingly willing to insist that someone else must rest.

facts.Care: Food, equipment and rest beside combat
facts.Status: Working at the Archery Range; joins the ongoing Vale investigation.

sources: Quest RP refreshed source · supplied 23 October 2026 · 3,845 messages across the main channel and two accessible threads; posting chronology and narrated continuations remain distinct
body:
Felicity repeatedly makes herself useful through work, preparation and care. Her deference does not keep her from danger, but choosing for herself can be harder than fighting.

A task at the funeral

At Papirak’s memorial, she places Cala’s statue where sunlight can fall upon it, following Pell’s request. She waits for work and checks that she has done it as intended. The act gives the room a small, deliberate form of remembrance.

Scene references: 1.

Composure in the night battle

She takes the first watch, fights from cover, heals companions and breaks the ambushers’ silence spell with an arrow. When the group calls for a prisoner, she tries to strike nonlethally. Her repeated apologies after missed attacks remain beside the narrator’s recognition of her resilience; they do not erase what she does accomplish.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Care becomes a decision

After the battle she helps pack the company’s equipment and discovers an unfamiliar magical stone. At the Dasa refuge she becomes firmer with the exhausted Saoirse, asks for a place to rest and guides her to food and a bed. She also learns the soup recipe, imagining food that travelers can carry and enjoy.

This is a bounded change in action, not proof that all her fear or practiced deference has disappeared. Follow the northern expedition →

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Working beside the people she serves

Felicity joins Di’trillio in clearing blocked drains and works with Vessalia’s cleaning magic. Her reluctance to let a noblewoman handle sewage exposes the hierarchy she brings to service. Di’trillio instead reminds her that they have fought on the same field and are now working side by side.

When her shadow visibly lags, she calls it Felicia and says it is not malignant. The observation and her explanation are distinct: the scene does not establish the shadow’s full nature. Plans to enlarge the drains or open etiquette lessons remain suggestions, while the shared cleaning is an action they actually take.

Teaching without forgetting the work

Felicity comes to the Archery Range to replace damaged targets and clear arrows, then stops to help Kage try a light shortbow. She demonstrates the stance and draw, and Kage’s first successful shot earns a gentle reminder that skill takes practice.

Clive calls the guidance overbearing, though Kage thanks her for the help. Felicity apologizes rather than arguing about her intention, then returns to sweeping up the dummy Clive has burned. Teaching and maintenance belong to the same service for her, even when her readiness to help is questioned.

Quiet questions in the Vale household

Felicity investigates Mara’s home with permission and follows Elias through the market in the manner of a maid doing ordinary shopping. Her questions to the florist are deliberately indirect. She respects his initial refusal to gossip and keeps listening until concern brings a little more information.

The task also unsettles her. She asks Saoirse why someone would pretend to love a person only to hurt them. At the memorial, she cleans the stones and asks whether Nhalis might be dead. The investigation gives her a chance to use the habits of service, but does not settle the personal questions those habits have carried into it.
